answer: A garden plot is licensed only beside a surveyed oasis whose water table two independent monitors gauge daily, and a new licence is granted when the table has recovered above a published mark. Every extra plot draws from the same recharge, so each licence lengthens the next one's wait by a full interval: the tenth plot waits ten intervals, the hundredth waits a hundred, and no payment shortens the gauge. Each boundary also carries stakes dyed with a pigment batch registered to that plot, so a stake lifted from one boundary fails the survey on another.
